summary: The Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship pays tuition, a return flight and a monthly allowance (¥143,000–145,000 for research students in the 2027 guidelines) for graduate study or research in Japan, usually starting with a non-degree 'research student' period. Nigerians apply through the Embassy of Japan in Abuja with a hard-copy application. Winners have a focused research plan that fits a real Japanese professor's lab, a strong academic record, and do well in the embassy's written tests and interview.
lookfor: A clear, feasible Field of Study and Research Program Plan that matches Japanese universities' strengths
Strong academic record shown in transcripts and the recommendation letter
Performance in the embassy's written exams (English and Japanese) and interview
Willingness to learn Japanese and ability to adapt to life in Japan
Good health (doctor-signed certificate in the official format)
Ability to get a provisional acceptance letter from a Japanese university
cycle: Nigeria's 2027 call opened in May 2026 and closed on 8 June 2026 (hard copy only); first screening ran May–July, university contact by 1 September, placement forms Sept–Oct, MEXT second screening in November and results Jan–Mar 2027 for April or Sept/Oct 2027 arrival. Expect the 2028 call around April–May 2027 on the Embassy of Japan in Nigeria website.

eligibility.q: Are you a national of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan, applying through the Japanese embassy in that country (for Nigerians: the Embassy in Abuja)?
eligibility.no: Apply through the Japanese embassy in your own country of nationality, or try the University Recommendation route with a Japanese university.

eligibility.q: Were you born on or after the cut-off date in the current guidelines (2 April 1992 for the 2027 research-student round)?
eligibility.no: You are over the MEXT age limit. Consider CSC (up to 40 for PhD) or GKS (under 40).

eligibility.q: Do you hold (or will you hold by the deadline) a bachelor's degree from at least 16 years of education, or a 3+ year degree treated as equivalent?
eligibility.no: Finish your degree first; final-year students need a certificate of prospective graduation.

eligibility.q: Are you willing to learn Japanese and live in Japan for the full award?
eligibility.no: MEXT expects this. If you cannot commit, choose another award.

eligibility.q: Are you free of military service and not already a MEXT recipient (or have you worked/studied 3+ years since)?
eligibility.no: Military personnel and recent MEXT scholars are ineligible.

eligibility.q: Do you plan to earn a degree in Japan?
eligibility.no: The 2027 guidelines list 'no intention of obtaining a degree in Japan' as ineligible for research students.

steps.title: Check you are eligible this round
steps.why: Age, degree and military rules are strict. The embassy rejects incomplete or ineligible applications without contact.
do: Open the Study in Japan 'Research Students' application page and download the current Application Guidelines PDF.
Find the birth-date cut-off and compare it with your birth certificate.
Read the 'ineligibility' list.
Open the Embassy of Japan in Nigeria MEXT notice and note the deadline and the address.
tips: Print the guidelines and highlight every 'must'.
avoid: Using last year's age cut-off; it moves by one year each round.
check: I meet the age and degree rules for this round.

steps.title: Understand how selection works
steps.why: MEXT has two big gates: the embassy's first screening (papers, exams, interview) and placement with a Japanese university.
do: Read the schedule table in the guidelines: first screening May–July, university contact by 1 September, placement form Sept–Oct, second screening November, results Jan–Mar.
Write each date in your calendar.
Compare with the University Recommendation route (via a Japanese university's partnership) as a backup.
Watch the past-applicant video on the Embassy Recommendation route below.
tips: The research plan is used at every stage – by the embassy, by professors and by MEXT.
avoid: Thinking the embassy interview is the last step; you still need a university to accept you.
check: I know the stages and their months.

steps.title: Find 3 Japanese universities and labs that fit your research
steps.why: Your plan must fit what Japanese universities can supervise; later you list up to three universities and may get up to two provisional acceptances.
do: Search Japanese university graduate school websites for professors in your field (use English 'faculty' or 'researchers' databases).
For each, note the professor's name, lab, recent papers and whether the course is taught in English.
Choose three that match your topic.
Fill in the Placement Preference Application Form draft with these choices.
tips: Choose universities across different tiers, not only the top three.
avoid: Picking a lab only for its fame when its topics do not match yours.
check: I have three labs whose work clearly matches my plan.

steps.title: Get transcripts and attested certificate copies
steps.why: The embassy rejects incomplete packs; you need originals plus copies, all years, with the grading scale shown.
do: Request transcripts for all years of study from your university's Exams & Records office; ask that the grading scale is printed.
Make copies of your degree certificate and have them attested (signed and stamped) by a university official, as the Nigerian notice requires.
If you have not graduated, request a certificate of prospective graduation.
Prepare the number of copies stated in the guidelines (original + 2 copies for most documents).
tips: Ask for several sealed transcripts at once; you may need them again for Japanese universities.
avoid: Sending your only original certificate; send attested copies as instructed.
check: I have every transcript and certificate in the required number of copies.

links.t: Watch: MEXT Embassy | Test & Interview Tips (Japan via Haris)

steps.title: Complete the medical certificate
steps.why: A doctor must sign the official MEXT Certificate of Health; a missing or self-made form makes you ineligible.
do: Download the 2027 Certificate of Health form from the Study in Japan page.
Take it to a hospital or clinic (a government or teaching hospital is safest); the doctor fills and signs it.
Check every box and the doctor's stamp are complete.
Make the required copies.
tips: Ask the clinic to do the chest X-ray and blood tests on the form the same day.
avoid: Filling parts the doctor must fill.
check: My medical form is signed and stamped by a physician.

steps.title: Add language certificates and thesis abstract
steps.why: Optional items strengthen your file: a recent IELTS/TOEFL/JLPT certificate, a thesis abstract, an employer letter if employed.
do: If you have an English or Japanese test certificate issued within two years, prepare it (3 copies).
Write a one-page abstract of your final-year or master's thesis, or attach a published paper's abstract.
If employed, request a free-format recommendation from your employer.
tips: Even basic JLPT N5 shows commitment to learning Japanese.
check: All optional documents I include are current and copied.

steps.title: Write the Field of Study and Research Program Plan
steps.why: It is the core of your application; the embassy, professors and MEXT all judge you on it.
steps.prompt: Describe your past and present field of study and the research theme you plan to pursue in Japan (official form).
steps.limit: Use the official form and its spaces; check the current form for any length instructions.
do: Start from the official form (download from Study in Japan); do not create your own layout.
Write your current field: degree, project, key results.
Write your research theme for Japan: title, background, problem, objectives.
Explain methods and why Japan (equipment, expertise, data).
Add a timeline across the scholarship years and the expected impact after you return.
Ask your supervisor to review it.
tips: Make it specific enough that a professor can tell in one minute if it fits their lab.
Keep the plan consistent with your three university choices.
avoid: A plan so broad it fits any lab.
check: A non-expert can understand my aim, method and why Japan.

links.t: How to write MEXT Field of study and research plan (Dr Sylvie Watikum)

steps.title: Get the recommendation letter
steps.why: MEXT requires a letter from your university president, dean or academic advisor (free format), original plus copies.
do: Ask your dean or project/thesis supervisor at least four weeks before the deadline.
Give them your research plan, CV and the deadline.
Ask for a signed letter on university letterhead, in English, dated recently.
Collect the original and make the required copies.
tips: Ask them to mention your rank in class or specific achievements.
avoid: Letters from family friends or people who never taught you.
check: I have a signed letter from my dean, president or advisor.

steps.title: Fill the Application Form and Placement Preference Form
steps.why: Mistakes or missing photos lead to rejection.
do: Download the 2027 Application Form and Placement Preference Form from the Study in Japan page.
Type your answers; names must match your passport.
Attach a recent photo (4.5 × 3.5 cm, taken within 6 months, no hat).
List your preferred universities consistently with your research plan.
Number all documents ① to ⑪ in the top right of the first page, as the guidelines say.
tips: Use the Embassy's checklist to order the pack.
avoid: Leaving boxes blank – write 'N/A' if not applicable.
check: Every form is signed and dated.

steps.title: Submit the hard-copy pack to the Embassy
steps.time: half a day (Abuja) or courier time
steps.why: Nigeria's 2027 call accepted only hard copies in person or by post; no email or online submission.
do: Arrange originals and copies in checklist order in an envelope.
Deliver in person or by courier to the Embassy of Japan in Nigeria (MEXT Selection Committee), Maitama, Abuja – use the exact address in the current notice.
Keep the courier tracking number or delivery receipt.
Keep a full photocopy of everything you sent.
tips: Send at least a week early from outside Abuja.
avoid: Emailing scans – they are not accepted.
check: I have proof of delivery before the deadline.

steps.title: Prepare for the written exams and interview
steps.why: The first screening includes written exams in English and Japanese and an interview; only successful candidates are contacted.
do: Both English and Japanese papers are compulsory. Practise English grammar and reading daily, and ask past Nigerian MEXT scholars what the papers looked like.
Learn basic Japanese (hiragana and katakana) – do your best on the Japanese paper even as a beginner.
Prepare a 2-minute summary of your research plan and answers to: Why Japan? Why this lab? What after?
Bring originals and your ID to the exam.
tips: Interviewers check that you wrote your plan yourself – know every detail.
avoid: Skipping the Japanese exam because you are a beginner.
check: I can explain my plan clearly in English in two minutes.

steps.title: Get a provisional acceptance letter from a Japanese professor
steps.why: Embassy-passed candidates must contact universities (by about 1 September) and may hold at most two provisional acceptances.
do: After the embassy tells you that you passed, email your chosen professors (no more than two at a time).
Attach your research plan, CV and the embassy's pass document; ask for a Letter of Provisional Acceptance.
Follow the professor's or university's procedure; some ask for an online interview.
Submit the Placement Preference Form with up to three universities by the embassy's date (mid-Sept–early Oct).
tips: Keep emails short and specific: who you are, your plan in 3 lines, why their lab.
avoid: Contacting more than two universities at the same time; the guidelines forbid it.
check: I have at least one provisional acceptance letter.

steps.title: Final results and travel to Japan
steps.why: MEXT confirms selection and university placement between January and March; you then arrive in April or September/October.
do: Watch for the embassy's message on final selection and placement.
Accept the placement and complete the university's admission steps.
Apply for the 'Student' visa with your Certificate of Eligibility at the Embassy.
Follow the embassy's travel instructions: MEXT sets the route and provides your economy ticket to Japan; you pay local travel and airport costs.
tips: Start learning Japanese daily; the first six months are often Japanese-language preparation.
avoid: Changing your residence status after arrival – it ends the scholarship.
check: I have my placement letter, visa and travel date.

faq.q: Can I apply online or by email in Nigeria?
faq.a: No. The 2027 Nigerian call accepted only hard copies in person or by post to the Embassy in Abuja.

faq.q: Do I need to speak Japanese?
faq.a: No, but you must be willing to learn it. You will sit a Japanese test at screening, and many scholars start with six months of Japanese.

faq.q: Do I need a professor's acceptance before applying?
faq.a: Not for the embassy route. You contact professors after passing the first screening.
The 2027 guidelines give ¥143,000 (non-regular research student), ¥144,000 (master's) and ¥145,000 (doctoral) per month, plus a small regional supplement in some areas.

faq.q: I missed the June deadline. What now?
faq.a: Prepare your research plan and documents now; the next Nigerian call is expected around April–May 2027.
The scholarship covers only you. The guidelines say housing for families is hard to find and ask grantees to arrive alone first, then bring dependants.
